Trace sound

The same trace demo, with the sound: the trajectory's shape path is heard as its spectrum (pointer-channels note §2–§5). Turn the sound on, then hover or tap. A periodic orbit is a note with timbre; chaos is noise. Pitch is derived from the system's crossing time, so two systems with the same frequency ratio sound like the same interval. Sweep a row to hear one basin become another.

Drag pans, wheel or pinch zooms, tap pins. The view goes past the chart's square with the controls shown: the sphere repeats by its θ period and over its poles, the latent planes continue, the simplex is blank past its edge (navigation stops when the centre would leave it, R-469).

Moving: a run to t = 20, so the sound is coarse. Dwell or tap: the run goes on to the horizon, trace and sound both, and it sharpens. Press Play: the trace draws out and the sound follows its head. A run ended early by its event is a short run, so a coarse spectrum.
